items.title: MBX v1.4: Memory-Aware SIMD-Enabled Permutationally Invariant Polynomial Code-Generation Procedure: Acceleration of the MB-pol Potential Energy Function as an Example.
items.authors: S. Iyer, E.F. Bull-Vulpe, C. Knight, F. Paesani
items.description: Permutationally invariant polynomial potential energy functions can deliver highly accurate many-body simulations, but molecular dynamics requires repeated evaluation of these polynomials and their gradients. This work introduces a memory-aware code-generation procedure that optimizes polynomial routines by extracting duplicate subexpressions and reordering statements to reduce the working set. Applied to the MB-pol potential energy function, the approach enables efficient SIMD vectorization and substantially accelerates polynomial evaluation with modern CPU instruction sets.

items.title: MBX v1.2: Accelerating data-driven many-body molecular dynamics simulations.
items.authors: S. Gupta, E.F. Bull-Vulpe, H. Agnew, S. Iyer, X. Zhu, R. Zhou, C. Knight, F. Paesani
items.description: The MBX software provides an advanced platform for molecular dynamics simulations, leveraging state-of-the-art MB-pol and MB-nrg data-driven many-body potential energy functions. Developed over the past decade, these potential energy functions integrate physics-based and machine-learned many-body terms trained on electronic structure data calculated at the “gold standard” coupled-cluster level of theory. Recent advancements in MBX have focused on optimizing its performance, resulting in the release of MBX v1.2. While the inherently many-body nature of MB-pol and MB-nrg ensures high accuracy, it poses computational challenges. MBX v1.2 addresses these challenges with significant performance improvements, including enhanced parallelism that fully harnesses the power of modern multicore CPUs. These advancements enable simulations on nanosecond time scales for condensed-phase systems, significantly expanding the scope of high-accuracy, predictive simulations of complex molecular systems powered by data-driven many-body potential energy functions.

items.title: MBX: A many-body energy and force calculator for data-driven many-body simulations.
items.authors: M. Riera, C. Knight, E.F. Bull-Vulpe, X. Zhu, H. Agnew, D.G.A. Smith, A.C. Simmonett, F. Paesani
items.description: Many-Body eXpansion (MBX) is a C++ library that implements many-body potential energy functions (PEFs) within the “many-body energy” (MB-nrg) formalism. MB-nrg PEFs integrate an underlying polarizable model with explicit machine-learned representations of many-body interactions to achieve chemical accuracy from the gas to the condensed phases. MBX can be employed either as a stand-alone package or as an energy/force engine that can be integrated with generic software for molecular dynamics and Monte Carlo simulations. MBX is parallelized internally using Open Multi-Processing and can utilize Message Passing Interface when available in interfaced molecular simulation software. MBX enables classical and quantum molecular simulations with MB-nrg PEFs, as well as hybrid simulations that combine conventional force fields and MB-nrg PEFs, for diverse systems ranging from small gas-phase clusters to aqueous solutions and molecular fluids to biomolecular systems and metal-organic frameworks.

applications_intro: MBX and the many-body expansion models behind it support a growing range of scientific applications and related methodological developments. The publications below highlight recent MBX-enabled research as well as derivative work that builds on the same data-driven many-body framework.

applications.title: Hydration Free Energies of Alkali Metal and Halide Ions from Data-Driven Many-Body Potentials.
applications.description: This work uses MB-nrg ion potentials in MB-pol water to calculate single-ion hydration free energies. A soft-core Coulomb scaling implemented in MBX enables robust alchemical transformations and a detailed separation of electrostatic, polarization, explicit many-body, and nuclear quantum contributions.

applications.title: From Potentials to Properties: Data-Driven Many-Body Simulations of Water and Aqueous Systems.
applications.authors: F. Paesani, R. Rashmi, H. Agnew, X. Zhu, E.F. Bull-Vulpe, R. Zhou
applications.description: This review surveys how MB-pol and MB-nrg data-driven many-body potential energy functions connect high-level electronic structure theory with predictive molecular simulations of water and aqueous systems across phases, interfaces, and chemical environments.

applications.title: Density-Functionalized QM/MM Delivers Chemical Accuracy For Solvated Systems.
applications.authors: X. Chen, J.A. Martinez B, X. Shao, M. Riera Riambau, O. Andreussi, F. Paesani, M. Pavanello
applications.description: A density-functionalized QM/MM framework assigns an electron density to both the quantum and molecular-mechanics subsystems and treats their interaction with orbital-free density functionals. Tests spanning water clusters, bulk water, solvated molecules and ions, and a wet MoS₂ monolayer demonstrate rapid convergence to chemical accuracy.

applications.title: Permutationally Invariant Fourier Series for Accurate and Robust Data-Driven Many-Body Potentials.
applications.description: Permutationally invariant Fourier series provide a robust representation of many-body potential energy functions that avoids unphysical low-energy holes outside the training domain while retaining high accuracy and computational efficiency.

applications.title: Sub-nanometer Confinement Suppresses Autoionization of Water.
applications.authors: S. Dasgupta, S. Saha, F. Paesani
applications.description: Density-corrected density functional theory and machine-learned interatomic potentials reveal that extreme confinement suppresses water autoionization by destabilizing hydroxide at interfaces and disrupting hydrogen-bond rearrangements and proton transport.
